examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution of a Second Order Differential Equation by Integrating Twice
examples.problem:
Solve the differential equation

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} = x.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Integrating the equation once, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating a second time, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+C)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\frac{1}{6}{x}^{3}+Cx+D\end{aligned}
$$

Note that because we had a second-order equation, our general solution contains *two* arbitrary constants, $C$ and $D.$ We cannot combine them, because $C$ is being multiplied by $x$ while $D$ is not.

feedback.problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation  ${f}^{′}(x)+6{x}^{2}=4x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation to isolate the derivative term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =4x-6{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (4x-6{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =4\int x\,\text{d}x-6\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-6\cdot \frac{1}{3}{x}^{3} \\  & =2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3}+C \\  & =2{x}^{2}(1-x)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
